item.title: Muslims will outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, report says
item.description: By 2070, the Democratic Republic of the Congo will surpass the United States as the country with the largest total number of Christians.

item.title: 'Huna' writer wins National Book Award for non-fiction, after not being allowed into the U.S.
item.description: Abdelrahman ElGendy published a recent essay about being denied a visa to enter the U.S. for the ceremony. His book is a memoir about his time as a political prisoner in Egypt.

item.title: Karl Kani dressed hip-hop royalty for decades. Now he's telling his own story
item.description: On NPR's Morning Edition, fashion designer Karl Kani talks about his new memoir, dressing some of hip-hop's biggest stars and why skinny jeans aren't for everyone.

item.title: For opera's Anthony Roth Costanzo, singing countertenor is a joyful catharsis
item.description: Costanzo is a countertenor — a man who can sing in the range of female voices. He sings opera and a Hawaiian song in our studio, and talks about his new memoir, which includes a history of castrati.

item.title: 'I Play Rocky' and 'Elsinore' can't land their punches, even with star performances
item.description: Two films harken back to previous Oscar-winning movies. Elsinore, set in 1989 London, centers on Ian Charleson, co-star of Chariots of Fire. I Play Rocky tells the origin story of Sly Stallone's hit.

item.title: Greetings from a Berlin square, where an artist's statue watches over children at play
item.description: Children frolic around the ever-watchful and calm Käthe Kollwitz cast in bronze, in a square named after the German artist, whose work often depicted children in the wake of World War I.

item.title: How the East Potomac golf course became a D.C. landmark — and what could happen to it
item.description: A federal judge is keeping East Potomac Park open for now, but hasn't ordered the government to keep the municipal golf course operational.

item.title: A Van Gogh could break auction records. An art recovery lawyer sees a darker history
